title: Unique normalized descent of a functor-square comparison
statement: For categories C,D,E,H,A,B,X,Y and functors q:C→D, p:E→H, k:C→E, t:C→A, s:E→B, Q:A→X, Qprime:B→Y, T:D→X, Tprime:H→Y, S:A→B, F:X→Y, G:D→H, suppose precomposition by q from functors D→Y to functors C→Y is fully faithful. Suppose given natural isomorphisms r:qT≅tQ, rprime:pTprime≅sQprime, epsilon:QF≅SQprime, eta:qG≅kp, and c:tSQprime≅ksQprime. Then there is a unique natural isomorphism alpha:TF≅GTprime with F(r_P) epsilon_(tP) c_P = alpha_(qP) Tprime(eta_P) rprime_(kP).

proof.text: On representatives, form a1 by applying F to r componentwise, a2 by whiskering epsilon by t, b1 by applying Tprime to eta componentwise, and b2 by whiskering rprime by k. Compose a1, a2, c, inverse b2 and inverse b1 to obtain the natural isomorphism between the restrictions of TF and GTprime. Lift it by FullyFaithful.preimageIso. The map-preimage equality and cancellation of isomorphisms prove the required normalized component square. For any other normalized alpha, cancel b1 and b2 in the two component equations. Faithfulness of restriction and extensionality of natural transformations then give equality of the isomorphisms. This also handles empty representative categories whenever restriction is fully faithful.

lean.statement:
theorem functorSquareRepresentativeDescent
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D]
    {E : Type uE} [Category.{vE} E] {H : Type uH} [Category.{vH} H]
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B]
    {X : Type uX} [Category.{vX} X] {Y : Type uY} [Category.{vY} Y]
    (q : C ⥤ D) (p : E ⥤ H) (k : C ⥤ E)
    (t : C ⥤ A) (s : E ⥤ B) (Q : A ⥤ X) (Q' : B ⥤ Y)
    (T : D ⥤ X) (T' : H ⥤ Y) (S : A ⥤ B) (F : X ⥤ Y) (G : D ⥤ H)
    (ff : ((Functor.whiskeringLeft C D Y).obj q).FullyFaithful)
    (r : q ⋙ T ≅ t ⋙ Q) (r' : p ⋙ T' ≅ s ⋙ Q')
    (ε : Q ⋙ F ≅ S ⋙ Q') (η : q ⋙ G ≅ k ⋙ p)
    (c : t ⋙ S ⋙ Q' ≅ k ⋙ s ⋙ Q') :
    ∃! α : T ⋙ F ≅ G ⋙ T', ∀ P : C,
      F.map (r.hom.app P) ≫ ε.hom.app (t.obj P) ≫ c.hom.app P =
        α.hom.app (q.obj P) ≫ T'.map (η.hom.app P) ≫ r'.hom.app (k.obj P)
